messages.subject: hierarchical parameter declaration and model comparison using LOOIC and WAIC
parts:
Professor Ahn，

First of all thank you for developing HBayesDM! It is really helpful, your HBayesDM make the stan code much easier for me.

Now,I have a few problems, I'm wondering whether you can give me some guide.
1. In my model I have parameters ranged from[-a,a](a>0),such as[-1,1],[-10,10].Can I declare hierarchical parameters in below way:
µξ′ ~ Normal(0, 1)
σξ′ ~ Cauchy(0, 5)
ξ' ~ Normal(µξ′, σ ξ′)
ξ = 2a*Probit-1 (ξ′)-a  

2. I use WAIC and LOOIC to do model comparison, however there were warnings ,which are most Pareto k diagnostic values are larger than 1. Does this mean I can't use WAIC and LOOIC to do model comparison?
And If I still can use WAIC and LOOIC  to do model comparison, how much difference of WAIC or LOOIC can prove a model is really better than another one.

                                                                                                                                                 All the best wishes!
                                                                                                                                                                Tong Yu

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: hierarchical parameter declaration and model comparison using LOOIC and WAIC
parts:
Thanks for the post!

1. Yes you can do that, but I wonder if you need such boundaries. And if you could upload your model here, it would be most helpful. If you prefer, you can email the code to me (wooyou...@gmail.com) and I can possibly add the model to the hBayesDM soon. 

2. I can comment on that but it would be most helpful if you check the following paper or ask it to the Stan mailing list directly. By the way, LOOIC is preferred to WAIC (between the two). 

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., & Gabry, J. (2015). Efficient implementation of leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC for evaluating fitted Bayesian models. arXiv preprint arXiv:1507.04544.

Hope this helps,
Young
